theorems.title: Known private-expansion transform and exact maximizer correspondence
theorems.primary_credit: Nie-Spiro, Random Turan Problems for Hypergraph Expansions, arXiv2408.03406v2, Lemma4.2 already gives the general uniform-hypergraph transform. Do not present the graph specialization as new mathematics.
theorems.quantifiers: For every finite simple graph G with at least two edges, every integer r>=2, and pairwise disjoint private vertex sets of size r-2 disjoint from V(G), its private expansion satisfies mr(G^[r])=m2(G)/(1+(r-2)m2(G)). No connectivity, bipartiteness, balance or Sidorenko assumption is required.
theorems.density_domain: ms(F)=max over actual subgraphs Q subset F with v(Q)>s of (e(Q)-1)/(v(Q)-s). It is undefined when this finite domain is empty. Vertices not incident with selected edges are allowed, and numerator subtraction is not truncated.
theorems.maximizer_statement: An eligible expanded subgraph attains positive mr iff it has at least two edges, has no vertex outside the union of its selected edges, and the corresponding actual core edges on their incident support attain m2(G). Thus the exact maximizing edge-subsets are independent of uniformity.
theorems.balance_statement: Whole-graph density-balancedness and density-strict-balancedness are each equivalent before and after private expansion. The cited paper's conventional strictness definition assumes at least three edges; our explicit two-edge statement extends the same density comparison literally.
proof: Two distinct simple graph edges have 3 or4 incident vertices, so m2(G)>0. Zero/one-edge selections cannot maximize. Adding a selected isolate strictly decreases a positive ratio.
Every f>=2 selected core-edge set with incident support v has expanded support cardinality v+(r-2)f and positive denominator v+(r-2)f-r.
Its expanded density is T_r(d2)=d2/(1+(r-2)d2). T_r is strictly increasing on positive values. Projection and expansion give both maximum inequalities and equality correspondence.
Whole-graph ratios transform by the same formula. A balanced graph with >=2edges cannot have isolates. Proper maximizers therefore correspond exactly, proving strictness equivalence.
degenerate_cases: One edge on n>=3vertices: both maxima are0; literal strict comparison holds exactly when n=3. Extra isolates beyond one yield proper zero-density maximizers.
Edgeless n>r: literal m2=-1/(n-2), mr=-1/(n-r); the formula holds but these negative values are not positive random extremal parameters.
Edgeless 3<=n<=r: m2 exists but mr does not; the formula cannot be asserted. At n=r its denominator would be zero.
K2 and its private expansion: both eligible-subgraph domains are empty under this definition; no zero convention is invented.
A forest with >=2edges and an adjacent pair has m2=1 and mr=1/(r-1). A matching with >=2edges has m2=1/2 and mr=1/r.
A connected tree with >=3edges is balanced but not strict, because a proper two-edge path maximizes. Two-edge trees and two-edge matchings satisfy the literal strict condition.
theorems.status: Complete analytical proof; known literature formula, useful actual-carrier/equality formalization target, not a new Lean result or novelty claim.

theorems.title: Spanning triangular exposure classes certify canonical balanced cores
theorems.quantifiers: For N>=1,t>=2, an indexed triangular family on the same N+2actualpointlabels is partitioned into t disjoint ordered classes, each with exactly Nfaces. Each face has3distinct points and every later face has a point absent from all previous faces of its class. Face labels are distinct; repeated pointsets across different classes are permitted. A simple triangular-complex realization is a subcase, not assumed to exist for every N,t.

conclusions.strict_two_density: m2=(3tN-1)/((t+1)N), equality only for the full actual incidence graph
conclusions.canonical_atom_scope: For r>=3, the bipartite2connectedcore shape is admitted as a single obligatory private-expansion atom by the higher-uniformity classification; its density inequality is NOT inferred.

proof: Exposure union lowerbound is N+2 and ambient size is N+2. Thus every class spans all points, and every face after the first introduces exactly one point and retains exactly two earlier points. This saturation is essential, not optional.

Deleting any point leaves each ordered class connected: initial face retains>=2points, later faces always retain an earlier attachment point. Deleting a face label leaves another full class connecting all points; every remaining face attaches to that backbone. Thus the full incidence graph is2vertexconnected.
For arbitrary selected point/face counts a,b, fully selected faces are <=t(a-2) when a>=2. Hence e<=min(3b,2b+t(a-2)); also e<=ab, a<=N+2,b<=tN. Non-induced selections only decrease e.
For a>=3 let x=a-2. If b<=tx, (3b-1)/(x+b) increases with b and is bounded by D_x=(3tx-1)/((t+1)x)<=D_N.
If b>=tx,t>=3, the other bound (2b+tx-1)/(x+b) is non-increasing in b, with derivative sign1-(t-2)x<=0; it is bounded by D_x. For t=2 it equals2-1/(x+b), bounded using x<=N,b<=2N.
Equality forces x=N,b=tN,e=3tN. The t=3,x=1 plateau first forces N=1 and then b=tN, so it gives no proper equality case.
Small point selections a0/1have negative/<=1density. For a2, density<=2-1/b<D_N, using b<=2N when t2 and D_N>=2 when t>=3. These discharge all eligible selected-subgraph cases.
tight_examples: N=1 is K3,t with indexed repeated triangles. This is a valid simple incidence graph, but NOT a distinct-triangle complex for t>=2.
N=2,t=2 can use all4triples on4points, partitioned into2two-face exposure classes; the incidence graph is the cube, with m2=11/6 and rank5.

Necessity diagnostic: on5points take2indexedclasses both ordered abc,ade. They are fresh and span all5points withN2, but are not saturated atN+2. Pointa is a cutvertex; wholegraph9vertices12edges hasdensity11/7, while the2abcfaces on3points have5vertices6edges anddensity5/3>11/7. Thus removing saturation can break both conclusions.

theorems.title: Unconditional random-host deletion benchmark
theorems.quantifiers: For fixed N,t,r and a fixed incidence-core expansion F from T2, let alpha=1/mr=r-2+(t+1)N/(3tN-1), gamma=r-alpha=2-(t+1)N/(3tN-1). G^r_n,rho has independent r-edge inclusion probability rho.
statements: If rho*n^alpha->0 and rho*n^r->infinity, a.a.s. ex(G^r_n,rho,F)=(1-o(1))*rho*binom(n,r).
For rho>=n^-alpha, independent thinning to rho'=n^-alpha/logn gives a.a.s. ex(G^r_n,rho,F)>=n^{gamma-o(1)}.
theorems.proof: Expected F-copy count divided by expected host-edge count is O(n^{v(F)-r}rho^{e(F)-1})=O((rho*n^alpha)^{e(F)-1}). Markov plus binomial edge concentration permit deleting one edge per remaining copy at o(1)edge loss. Above the deletion scale, randomized thinning has near-full retained edge count n^gamma/logn with high joint probability, implying an existential F-free subgraph for a.a.s. original hosts.
theorems.scope: No Sidorenko excess, kernel counterexample, positive gain or matching upper bound is assumed. This is a deletion/near-full-retention scale, NOT the first-appearance threshold. gamma is independent of uniformity by the known expansion transform.
theorems.status: Elementary complete analytical benchmark, not a new probabilistic theorem or Lean acceptance.
